```{r}
#| label: helpers

# ---- Path diagram (replaces the tikz mediation diagrams) --------------------
# Boxes, arrows, and plotmath labels drawn in ggplot. `captions` are plotmath
# strings (use ~ for spaces) placed under the left and right diagrams.
path_diagram <- function(captions = c("Single~Mediator~Model", "Regression~Model"),
                         txt_size = 6.5) {
  boxes <- data.frame(
    xmin = c(2, 0, 4, 6.5, 10), xmax = c(4, 2, 6, 8.5, 12),
    ymin = c(2.5, 1, 1, 1, 1),  ymax = c(3.5, 2, 2, 2, 2),
    label = c("Mediator~italic(m)", "Predictor~italic(x)", "Outcome~italic(y)",
              "Predictor~italic(x)", "Outcome~italic(y)")
  )
  arrows <- data.frame(x = c(1, 4, 2, 8.5), y = c(2, 3, 1.5, 1.5),
                       xend = c(2, 5, 4, 10), yend = c(3, 2, 1.5, 1.5))
  path_labs <- data.frame(x = c(1.2, 4.85, 3, 9.25), y = c(2.75, 2.75, 1.78, 1.78),
                          label = c("hat(a)", "hat(b)", "hat(c)*minute", "hat(c)"))
  caps <- data.frame(x = c(3, 9.25), y = 0.55, label = captions)

  ggplot() +
    geom_rect(data = boxes, aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax),
              fill = NA, colour = "black", linewidth = 1) +
    geom_text(data = boxes, aes(x = (xmin + xmax) / 2, y = (ymin + ymax) / 2, label = label),
              parse = TRUE, size = txt_size) +
    geom_segment(data = arrows, aes(x = x, y = y, xend = xend, yend = yend),
                 arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.3, "cm"), type = "open"), linewidth = 1) +
    geom_text(data = path_labs, aes(x = x, y = y, label = label),
              parse = TRUE, size = txt_size) +
    geom_text(data = caps, aes(x = x, y = y, label = label),
              parse = TRUE, size = txt_size) +
    coord_fixed(xlim = c(-0.1, 12.1), ylim = c(0.2, 3.7), clip = "off") +
    theme_void()
}

# ---- Regression surfaces for the moderation slide ---------------------------
reg_surface <- function(f, rows) {
  x1 <- seq(0, 1, length = 20)
  x2 <- seq(0, 1, length = 20)
  y <- outer(x1, x2, f)
  pal <- colorRampPalette(c(my_red, my_blue))(20)
  z.facet.center <- (y[-1, -1] + y[-1, -ncol(y)] + y[-nrow(y), -1] + y[-nrow(y), -ncol(y)]) / 4
  z.facet.range <- cut(z.facet.center, 20)
  pmat <- persp(x = x1, y = x2, z = y, theta = -30, box = TRUE, axes = TRUE,
                ticktype = "simple", col = pal[z.facet.range],
                xlab = "x", ylab = "z", zlab = "y", cex.lab = 1.5)
  for (r in rows) {
    lines(trans3d(x = x1, y = rep(x2[r], 20), z = y[, r], pmat = pmat),
          col = my_orange, lwd = 5)
  }
}

# ---- Annotated console output (replaces tikz rectangles drawn over output) ---
# Prints `lines` as a block of text, draws a coloured outline around the
# `highlight` line(s), and puts `label` (HTML) beside the first highlighted line.
html_output <- function(lines, highlight = NULL, label = NULL, color = my_orange, lh = 1.35) {
  esc <- function(s) {
    s <- gsub("&", "&amp;", s, fixed = TRUE)
    s <- gsub("<", "&lt;", s, fixed = TRUE)
    gsub(">", "&gt;", s, fixed = TRUE)
  }
  rows <- vapply(seq_along(lines), function(i) {
    txt <- if (nzchar(lines[i])) esc(lines[i]) else "&nbsp;"
    outline <- if (i %in% highlight) {
      sprintf("outline: 3px solid %s; outline-offset: -1px;", color)
    } else ""
    sprintf("<span style='display:block; white-space:pre; line-height:%sem; %s'>%s</span>",
            lh, outline, txt)
  }, character(1))
  lab <- ""
  if (!is.null(label) && length(highlight) > 0) {
    top <- 0.4 + (highlight[1] - 1) * lh
    lab <- sprintf(paste0("<div style='position:absolute; left:100%%; margin-left:1em; ",
                          "top:%sem; height:%sem; display:flex; align-items:center; ",
                          "white-space:nowrap; color:%s; font-size:0.9em; line-height:1.1;'>%s</div>"),
                   top, lh, color, label)
  }
  html <- paste0("<div style='position:relative; display:inline-block; margin-right:10em;'>",
                 "<pre class='sh' style='margin:0; padding:0.4em 0.6em; font-size:1em; overflow:visible;'>",
                 "<code>", paste(rows, collapse = ""), "</code></pre>", lab, "</div>")
  cat("\n```{=html}\n", html, "\n```\n", sep = "")
}
```

## Polynomial Regression


::: {style="font-size: 0.7em;"}


Polynomial equations:

$$\begin{aligned}
\hat{y} &= b_{0}+b_{1}x &&\quad \text{1st order polynomial (linear)}\\
\hat{y} &= b_{0}+b_{1}x+b_{2}x^{2} &&\quad \text{2nd order polynomial (quadratic)}\\
\hat{y} &= b_{0}+b_{1}x+b_{2}x^{2}+b_{3}x^{3} &&\quad \text{3rd order polynomial (cubic)}\\
\hat{y} &= b_{0}+b_{1}x+b_{2}x^{2}+\cdots+b_{p}x^{p} &&\quad p\text{th order polynomial}
\end{aligned}$$

- Always include all "lower order" terms
- A polynomial of order $p$ has $(p-1)$ bends or inflections 

$p = 1$ has no bends (straight line)

Quadratic polynomial:

- One bend
- $b_2$: quadratic effect
- $b_2 > 0$: curve is concave up
- $b_2 < 0$: curve is concave down

:::

## Quadratic Model Viz

```{r}
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 5.5

quad_dat <- data.frame(x = seq(-2, 2, by = .01))
quad_dat <- rbind(
  data.frame(x = quad_dat$x, y = quad_dat$x^2,     type = "concave up"),
  data.frame(x = quad_dat$x, y = 4 - quad_dat$x^2, type = "concave down")
)

# Replaces the tikz overlay nodes: one label per facet
quad_labs <- data.frame(type = c("concave down", "concave up"),
                        x = 0, y = 3,
                        label = c("b[2] == -1", "b[2] == 1"))

ggplot(quad_dat, aes(x, y)) + 
  geom_line(col = my_blue, linewidth = 2) + 
  geom_text(data = quad_labs, aes(label = label), parse = TRUE, 
            col = my_blue, size = 11) +
  facet_wrap(~type) + 
  theme_minimal(base_size = 18) + 
  labs(x = "", y = "") + 
  theme(strip.text.x = element_text(size = 22))
```


## Cubic Model Viz



```{r}
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 6.5

b2_vals <- c(1, -1)
b3_vals <- c(1, -1)

cubic_dat <- expand.grid(x = seq(-2, 2, by = .01), b2 = b2_vals, b3 = b3_vals)
cubic_dat$y <- with(cubic_dat, b2 * x^2 + b3 * x^3)   # b0 = b1 = 0 so the bends are easy to see

# Parsed facet labels replace the tikz overlay nodes
cubic_dat$b2_lab <- factor(cubic_dat$b2, levels = b2_vals,
                           labels = paste0("b[2] == ", b2_vals))
cubic_dat$b3_lab <- factor(cubic_dat$b3, levels = b3_vals,
                           labels = paste0("b[3] == ", b3_vals))

ggplot(cubic_dat, aes(x, y)) + 
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, col = "grey80") +
  geom_line(col = my_blue, linewidth = 2) + 
  facet_grid(b3_lab ~ b2_lab, labeller = label_parsed) + 
  theme_minimal(base_size = 18) + 
  labs(x = "", y = "") + 
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 22))
```



## Centering


::: {style="font-size: 0.7em;"}


Two options for setting up $x$ in the equation:

$$\begin{aligned}
\hat{y} &= b_{0}+b_{1}x+b_{2}x^{2} &&\quad \text{uncentered equation}\\
\hat{y} &= b_{0}+b_{1}(x-\bar{x})+b_{2}(x-\bar{x})^{2} &&\quad \text{centered equation}
\end{aligned}$$

Regression coefficients between uncentered and centered equations:

- $b_2$: second-order coefficient (quadratic effect)
  - Both equations have exactly the same $b_2$ coefficient, standard error of $b_2$, and $t$-test

- $b_1$: first-order coefficient
  - $b_1$ differs between the uncentered and centered equations
  - $b_1$ depends on the scaling of $b_2$

- $b_0$: regression constant (intercept)
  - $b_0$ differs between the uncentered and centered equations
  - $b_0$ depends on the scaling of $b_2$

Note: no need to center the outcome $y$

:::

## Centering and Colinearity


::: {style="font-size: 0.75em;"}

Using centered $x$ eliminates a potential computational difficulty (depending on the accuracy of your software/computer)

- collinearity between $x$ and $x^2$

Example:

::: columns

:::: {.column width="50%"}

| $x$ | $x^{2}$ | $(x-\bar{x})$ | $(x-\bar{x})^{2}$ |
|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| 1 | 1  | -3 | 9 |
| 3 | 9  | -1 | 1 |
| 5 | 25 | 1  | 1 |
| 7 | 49 | 3  | 9 |

::::

:::: {.column width="50%"}

$$\begin{aligned}
\text{cor}(x, x^2) &= .98\\
\text{cor}[(x - \bar{x}), (x - \bar{x})^2] &= 0
\end{aligned}$$

::::

:::

- Merely changing the scale of $x$ dramatically changes $\text{cor}(x, x^2)$
  
- The correlation that is produced merely by scaling is called **non-essential multicollinearity**
  
- If $x$ is symmetric, $(x - \bar{x})$ and $(x - \bar{x})^2$ will have zero correlation
  
- If $x$ is skewed, $(x - \bar{x})$ and $(x - \bar{x})^2$ will have non-zero correlation

:::

## Example



Example: College graduation rates as a function of the percentage of the population that is black among Minneapolis neighborhoods in 2015


```{r}
#| echo: true
mod1 <- lm(collegeGrad ~ black, MplsDemo)
summary(mod1)
```

## Linear Interpretations

No quadratic $x$: 

```{r}
options(width = 80)
round(summary(mod1)$coefficients, 4)
```



$$\hat{y} = .64 - 1.01x$$

- $b_1 = -1.01$: **linear** regression of collegeGrad ($y$) on black ($x$)
- $b_0 = .63$: average predicted value of collegeGrad at black = 0



## Linear Visual

```{r}

ggplot(MplsDemo, aes(black, collegeGrad)) + geom_point() + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, formula = y ~ x, col = my_blue) + 
  labs(title = "Linear Model") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 16)

```


## Quadratic Example {.scrollable}

The `^` operator has a special function that is not "raise to the power of" when used inside `R`'s formula syntax. To "inhibit" this special meaning, we need to wrap the quadratic term around `I()`

```{r}
#| echo: true
mod2 <- lm(collegeGrad ~ black + I(black^2), MplsDemo)
summary(mod2)
```

## Quadratic Interpretations

Uncentered $x$: 

```{r}
options(width = 80)
round(summary(mod2)$coefficients, 4)
```



$$\hat{y} = .70 - 1.89x + 1.75x^2$$

- $b_1 = -1.89$: linear regression of collegeGrad ($y$) on black ($x$) **at black = 0**
  - Because in quadratic model slope changes as $x$ changes
- $b_0 = .70$: average predicted value of collegeGrad at black = 0


## Quadratic Visual

```{r}
# Label sits just right of the dotted line, at the bottom of the plot
mean_label <- function(xint) {
  annotate("text", x = xint, y = min(MplsDemo$collegeGrad),
           label = "Mean of black", hjust = -0.1, vjust = 0, size = 5.5)
}

ggplot(MplsDemo, aes(black, collegeGrad)) + geom_point() + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, formula = y ~ x + I(x^2), col = my_blue) + 
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean(MplsDemo$black), linetype = 3) +
  mean_label(mean(MplsDemo$black)) +
  labs(title = "Uncentered Model") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 16)
```


## Centered Model {.scrollable}

```{r}
#| echo: true
MplsDemo <- MplsDemo |>
  mutate(black_centered = black - mean(black))

mod3 <- lm(collegeGrad ~ black_centered + I(black_centered^2), MplsDemo)
summary(mod3)
```





## Centered Interpretations


Centered $x$:

$$\hat{y} = .44 - 1.32(x - \bar{x}) + 1.75(x - \bar{x})^2$$

- $b_1 = -1.32$: average linear regression of collegeGrad on black **across the range of black**
- $b_0 = .44$: predicted value of collegeGrad at the average value of black

```{r}
round(summary(mod3)$coefficients, 4)
options(width = 60)
```


## Centered Visual

```{r}

 ggplot(MplsDemo, aes(black_centered, collegeGrad)) + geom_point() + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, formula = y ~ x + I(x^2), col = my_blue) + 
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean(MplsDemo$black_centered), linetype = 3) +
  mean_label(mean(MplsDemo$black_centered)) +
  labs(title = "Centered Model") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 16)

```





## Interpretations



Uncentered $x$: 

$$\hat{y} = .70 - 1.89x + 1.75x^2$$



Centered $x$:

$$\hat{y} = .44 - 1.32(x - \bar{x}) + 1.75(x - \bar{x})^2$$



**Both Models:**

$b_2 = 1.75$: curve is concave up
